# Why Izanagi is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *izanagi*. This is the file on how **Izanagi** replaced it.

Izanagi's mythology is the creation narrative of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki: the making of the world, the founding of death, and the birth of the gods who rule heaven and earth.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Izanagi
- **ASCII form:** izanagi
- **Meaning:** "He who invites"
- **Domain of influence:** Creator God, Shintō
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** 伊邪那岐
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 204 of 449

## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **伊邪那岐**, on the evidence Kojiki (creation, Yomi, purification) and Nihon Shoki (parallel creation accounts) set down. On the evidence, it means "He who invites".


Spoken, the name runs `/i.za.na.ɡi/` — 'EE-zah-nah-gee' — the 'g' is hard, and the 'r' of Western transcriptions is absent in Japanese.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Izanagi** lives at [/izanagi/](/izanagi/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/izanagi/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/izanagi/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/izanagi/patterns/).

The restoration keeps one feature the ASCII form drops. One is enough to matter, and the label says so plainly: Tier-2.

## Where the Name Stood First

Izanagi has no independent material cult separate from shrines honoring the creation kami as a pair. The Taga Taisha in Ōmi is one prominent shrine associated with Izanagi and Izanami. Creation imagery appears in shrine art and ritual objects across Japan. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** (the male creator who stirred the primordial brine and gave birth to the islands.); **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** (the creator who organized the islands and the pantheon; primordial executive authority.); **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** (the creator's footsteps formed the Japanese islands; the myth is the itinerary.). The [Resonance File](/izanagi/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Japanese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/) and [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
